name: MaZiRenWan (Hemp Seed Pill, Chinese herbal formula)
short: Placebo-controlled trial (120 people with constipation, by mouth): no serious adverse events; 17-trial review: adverse events not increased. Abstracts give no event types or counts.
text: MaZiRenWan (Hemp Seed Pill) is a Chinese herbal formula taken by mouth; a review of herbal laxatives names rhubarb as a key ingredient, and the cited trial abstracts do not list its herbs. In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 120 people with functional constipation (60 per group), with 8 weeks of treatment and 8 weeks of follow-up, no serious adverse event was reported; the abstract does not say whether milder adverse events occurred. In a double-blind, double-dummy trial in 291 people with functional constipation that compared the formula with the stimulant laxative senna and with placebo for 8 weeks, adverse events were collected and the authors describe the formula as well tolerated, but the abstract gives no adverse-event figures. A 2021 systematic review of 17 trials (1681 patients, moderate-to-high risk of bias, all in east Asia) found that use of the formula did not increase adverse events compared with not using it (p = 0.99). In a pilot placebo-controlled trial in 60 people with advanced cancer (mean age 75.2, range 47 to 95), a modified version of the formula, adjusted for each patient, was given with their current prescriptions, including laxatives, for two weeks, and no serious adverse event was reported due to the research medication; this is a different, individualised preparation. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
